title: Immunostimulatory activity of sea buckthorn polysaccharides via TLR2/4-mediated MAPK and NF-kappaB signaling pathways in vitro and in vivo.
authors: Tian, Haiyan; Ling, Na; Guo, Chunqiu; Gao, Mingze; Wang, Zihao; Liu, Bing; Sun, Yuan; Chen, Yin; Ji, Chenfeng; Li, Wenlan
one_liner_zh: 研究沙棘多糖通过TLR2/4介导的MAPK和NF-κB信号通路的免疫刺激活性，涉及分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: SP0.1-1, derived from Sea buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides L.), has been discovered to exhibit unique antioxidant activity. In this study, we investigated the immunomodulatory activity and mechanisms of SP0.1-1 on macrophage RAW 264.7 cells in vitro and immunosuppressive mice induced by cyclophosphamide in vivo. The results indicated SP0.1-1 strengthened the immune functions via promoting the proliferation of RAW264.7 cells and phagocytic activity, along with stimulating the release of NO, ROS and cytokines including TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-1beta and IFN-gamma. Western blot and molecular docking analysis demonstrated that SP0.1-1 attached to the prime receptors TLR2 and TLR4 in RAW264.7 cells, and triggered the activation of MyD88-mediated MAPK and NF-kappaB signaling pathways, thereby exerting the immune response in RAW264.7 cells. However, the intervention of specific inhibitors against TLR2, TLR4, JNK, ERK, p38 and NF-kappaB blocked the TLR-mediated MAPK and NF-kappaB signaling pathways and downregulated the levels of NO and the aforementioned cytokines, thus suppressing the activation of macrophages. Therefore, it can be speculated that SP0.1-1 activated the macrophages principally via the TLR2/4-MyD88-mediated MAPK and NF-kappaB signaling pathways. Additionally, SP0.1-1 could protect against the cyclophosphamide-induced immunosuppression in mice, manifested by the improvement of body weight, immune organ indices, phagocytic index, and the relievement of spleen damage, along with the enhancement of cytokines TNF-alpha, IL-6, IFN-gamma and immunoglobulin IgG and IgM. These findings will shed light on the molecular mechanism of SP0.1-1 on the immunoregulatory effect, and lay the foundation for exploiting a potential immunostimulatory agent of SP0.1-1.
abstract_zh: SP0.1-1，源自沙棘（Hippophae rhamnoides L.），已被发现具有独特的抗氧化活性。在本研究中，我们探讨了SP0.1-1对巨噬细胞RAW 264.7的体外免疫调节活性及其机制，以及由环磷酰胺诱导的体内免疫抑制小鼠模型。结果表明，SP0.1-1通过促进RAW264.7细胞的增殖和吞噬活性，并刺激NO、ROS及细胞因子（包括TNF-alpha、IL-6、IL-1beta和IFN-gamma）的释放，增强了免疫功能。Western blot和分子对接分析显示，SP0.1-1附着于RAW264.7细胞中的主要受体TLR2和TLR4，并触发MyD88介导的MAPK和NF-kappaB信号通路的激活，从而在RAW264.7细胞中发挥免疫应答。然而，针对TLR2、TLR4、JNK、ERK、p38和NF-kappaB的特异性抑制剂干预，阻断了TLR介导的MAPK和NF-kappaB信号通路，并下调了NO及上述细胞因子的水平，从而抑制了巨噬细胞的活化。因此，可以推测SP0.1-1主要通过TLR2/4-MyD88介导的MAPK和NF-kappaB信号通路激活巨噬细胞。此外，SP0.1-1能够保护小鼠免受环磷酰胺诱导的免疫抑制，表现为体重、免疫器官指数、吞噬指数的改善，脾脏损伤的缓解，以及细胞因子TNF-alpha、IL-6、IFN-gamma和免疫球蛋白IgG、IgM的增强。这些发现将揭示SP0.1-1免疫调节效应的分子机制，并为开发SP0.1-1作为潜在免疫刺激剂奠定基础。
